brief: Verdict ahead of the print: the ramp should show; CoreWeave credit and AMD funding will drive the stock.
Kona: benchmark on build cost per MW and tenant credit support.
changes: Report date set: before the open on 5 November 2026, call 8:30 a.m. ET.
Needham (14 October): management said sector spreads widened more than expected and a stock offering is possible but raises the bar for new projects.
$600mn credit package closed in August, freeing about $300mn of restricted cash (Needham note).
Cantor cut its target to $30 from $39; KBW cut again on 2 November.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Core Scientific as a colocation landlord with about 1.1 GW leased and over $24bn of potential contracted revenue, moving from CoreWeave-only to AMD-backed tenancy. At $12.90 on 2 November (about $4.1bn on 321.34mn shares), the market prices doubt over CoreWeave credit, whose CDS were back above 800 bps in September, and over funding of the AMD build. Positioning is contested: about 27% of float short, while targets run from Cantor's $30 to Needham's $35. The 7.75% 2031 secured notes are the last price point; no current quote was found.
headline: 3Q26 revenue (consensus about $197mn) should reflect the CoreWeave ramp, but the stock and credit will trade on CoreWeave exposure, how the $6bn AMD build is financed as spreads widen, and whether equity is needed near $13 a share.
kona: Core Scientific's AMD deal at $11mn to $12mn per MW, financed mainly with project bonds, is a current build-cost and structure benchmark. Its AMD credit support for a neocloud tenant (about 150 MW, 15 years, no equity step-in rights) shows how a smaller operator can borrow a stronger balance sheet, a structure Kona could seek for a non-investment-grade tenant.
monitor: MW billing at 30 September against 437 MW in mid-July and the 590 MW CoreWeave total.
AMD project financing: size, price, recourse and timing, and any equity.
Dalton Phase Two start at year-end and Pecos in 1H27.
name: Core Scientific

questions.question: CoreWeave was about 77% of first-half revenue and its CDS traded above 800 bps in September, and your 10-Q says recourse depends on its condition at default. What would you do with 590 MW if it missed a payment, how long to re-lease, and what do the 7.75% notes' terms require?
questions.why: Decides whether the secured notes rest on the site or the tenant.

questions.question: You told Needham spreads widened more than expected. What yield would the first AMD project bond clear at today, what advance rate on $11mn to $12mn per MW, and how much parent equity for 530 MW? Will you issue common stock near $13?
questions.why: Funding cost against lease yield decides whether growth adds value.

questions.question: You guided a 'meaningful step-up' in billing. How many MW billed on 30 September and today, and on what dates does Dalton Phase Two start and finish?
questions.why: Direct test of management's delivery record.

questions.question: Is any covenant tied to market cap or liquidity, and at today's price how much headroom do you have?
questions.why: A covenant near the current cap would bind funding.

questions.question: AMD has reservation rights on up to 2 GW. How long do they last, is anything paid, and when would capacity revert if unused?

risks: AMD financing at wider spreads; equity need.

sections.body: Converted mining sites into colocation. Rent = billing MW x $/kW-month. CoreWeave leases 590 MW across six sites; AMD leases 377 MW directly and supports 152 MW for a neocloud over 15 years, about $14bn of base revenue, with reservation rights on up to 2 GW more. Mining is winding down; management calls 2027 a clean year.
